thread:
Maria (CS): Quick async pulse from my side — customer BlueHarbor renewal in two weeks. Yesterday: did account health review and saw webhook delivery failure spike for their ingestion route, which correlates with a 12% drop in adoption events.

Maria (CS): Today: I tried the usual workarounds (resend, temporary webhook toggle) but the queue keeps backing up. Blocker: we need a small infra tweak or config to stop retries flooding the upstream.

Devon (SE): Can you dump the last 20 error lines?

Maria (CS): paste below — this is from their callback logs around 08:42 UTC:

```
[2026-03-16T08:42:12Z] ERROR POST /callbacks/ingest 500 upstream="model-router-prod" x-request-id=abc123
[2026-03-16T08:42:12Z] WARN retrying webhook (attempt 4) for customer=blueharbor delay=2000ms
[2026-03-16T08:42:13Z] ERROR POST /callbacks/ingest 429 upstream="billing-proxy" x-request-id=abc124
[2026-03-16T08:42:15Z] ERROR POST /callbacks/ingest 500 upstream="model-router-prod" x-request-id=abc125
```

Aj (Eng): 429 from billing-proxy + 500 from model-router — looks like retries are amplifying transient upstream rate limits. We should: 1) increase jitter/backoff for webhook retryer, 2) short-circuit retries on repeated 429s for same x-request-id, 3) add a temporary route override to drop retries for BlueHarbor while we investigate.

Sam (Infra): I can flip a temporary feature flag at the edge to stop automatic retries for that customer. Will need a quick PR to the edge-config service (tiny change).

Becky (PM): If we can stop retries today, that reduces visible throttling and should let the renewal call go ahead. Keep me posted — I have a sync with BlueHarbor in 90m.

Devon (SE): Aj — want me to draft the PR? I can add the config key: `edge.retry_policy.customers.blacklist = ["blueharbor"]` and a note.

Aj (Eng): Please do. Minimal tests: verify that the edge returns 202 for accepted but does not enqueue retry when in blacklist. I'll review.

Maria (CS): Workaround I did manually: toggled customer-level webhook retries off from the CS console for testing — command I used in case helpful:

```
curl -X POST "https://console.internal.redwood/api/customers/blueharbor/actions" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"action":"set_webhook_retry","value":false}'
```

Maria (CS): That reduced repeated 429s but not the 500 bursts. We need the edge change + Aj to look at model-router 500s separately.

Oncall Bot: Reminder: incident runbook link https://internal.redwood/runbooks/webhook-bulk-retry :owner=@Devon (SE) :status=investigating

Sam (Infra): I'll open the edge-config PR and set a deploy canary window for 30m, then monitor.

Devon (SE): PR opened: https://git.internal.redwood/edge-config/pulls/482 — changes + unit test. pinging @Aj (Eng) for review.

Aj (Eng): Reviewing now, quick comments left. Should be safe for canary.

Maria (CS): Thanks team — immediate ask: if PR merges, can we enable the canary before my 90m call with BlueHarbor? If yes I'll tell them we're putting in a mitigation.

Aj (Eng): If review clears in 20–30m we can canary in the morning window. I'll prioritize.

Becky (PM): +1, please update this thread with canary status so I can share in the renewal sync.

Maria (CS): Will do. Also: action item for post-mitigation — run an adoption regressions check and annotate any missing events tied to retries so we can present to the customer.

Devon (SE): Noted. I'll add a small smoke test to the PR to assert no retry enqueue for blacklisted customers and attach the results.

Maria (CS): Thanks everyone. If anything changes I'll ping here. :thumbsup:

Oncall Bot: deploy/edge-config-pr-482 canary started by @Sam (Infra) — monitoring for 15m: https://deploys.internal.redwood/edge-config/482/canary
